name: Soy isoflavones
short: Meta-analyses of trials found no oestrogen-like effect on the womb lining or hormone levels in postmenopausal women; soy very modestly raised TSH without changing thyroid hormones.
text: A meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials (3285 postmenopausal women; median 24 weeks) found that soy isoflavones had no statistically significant effect on four measures of oestrogenic activity, including thickness of the womb lining and blood oestradiol. A meta-analysis of randomised trials of soy and thyroid function (18 articles) found no significant change in the thyroid hormones free T3 and free T4 but a very modest rise in TSH, whose clinical significance, if any, the authors called unclear. An earlier safety review noted that negative effects have been postulated because of the oestrogenic activity of isoflavones and that results in some studies are limited or conflicting, but concluded that the literature as a whole supports the safety of isoflavones as typically consumed in soy-based diets. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
